title: Heating and cooling changes
keyIdea: Heating can melt a solid and boil a liquid; cooling can freeze a liquid; we measure the temperature in °C.

kid: Heat chocolate and it melts. Put water in the freezer and it turns to ice.
A thermometer tells us how hot or cold something is, in degrees (°C).
adult: Each material changes state at its own temperature. Water melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C. Chocolate melts at about 34 °C, which is why it melts in a warm hand.
Heating moves along solid → liquid → gas; cooling goes back. Reading a thermometer at the moment of change is a good first science measurement.

familyTip: Put a square of chocolate in your hand and one on a cold plate. Which melts first? Why?

practice.prompt: Water is at {t} °C. How many degrees warmer until it boils at 100 °C?
Room is {t} °C. Chocolate melts at 34 °C. How many degrees warmer?
